clue.text: One enthralled having got back care of painting

indicators.note: having got back tells us the word for a person in thrall is written in reverse

parts.note: a serf is one held in bondage, enthralled in the old sense
c/o, written CO, is the postal abbreviation for care of

explanation.surface: Someone captivated by a painting is getting their care back from it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having got back' turns SERF into FRES; 'enthralled' is meant in its old sense of enslaved, not charmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a kind of painting done on wet plaster walls.

clue.text: Section of choir on Donizetti's musical piece

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of a choral work by the opera composer Donizetti.
explanation.definitionFit: A rondo is a musical form in which a main theme keeps returning.

clue.text: Updates inhibiting support for raising bribe

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising means the letters are read upwards, so backwards
inhibiting means holding in, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: renews means brings up to date
a tee supports a golf ball

explanation.surface: News updates restrain backing for a fundraising bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion makes RENETEEWS; 'for raising' then reads it upwards, as a down clue is read from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetener is slang for an inducement or backhander paid to win favour.

clue.text: Shop at fault with unsatisfactory service

parts.note: out means mistaken, as in your figures are out
in tennis a let is a serve that clips the net and must be replayed

explanation.surface: A store blamed for poor customer service.
explanation.definitionFit: An outlet is a retail store, especially one selling a maker's goods.

clue.text: One thinks about industrial city familiarly after church

indicators.note: after places the pieces about the city following the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
re means concerning
Brum is the nickname for Birmingham, the English industrial city

explanation.surface: Someone contemplating Birmingham, by its nickname, after a visit to church.
explanation.walkthrough: BRUM is the familiar name for Birmingham, a big industrial city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The cerebrum is the main part of the brain, the organ that does the thinking.

clue.text: In this case, yours truly's record set's worst being scratched

definitions.note: the setter speaking of themselves: in a crossword, I am the compiler

indicators.note: a scratched record is damaged, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The setter admits their worst record has been scratched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yours truly's' means 'yours truly is': the compiler of this puzzle is the one speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: The person writing a puzzle refers to themselves, so here the speaker is its compiler.

clue.text: Quit terrible sin — greed

indicators.note: terrible suggests something wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone stepped down after a dreadful case of greed.
explanation.definitionFit: Resigned is the past tense of leaving a post, the same as quit.

clue.text: Injunction about to stick

indicators.note: about means around, so the ban surrounds the word to

parts.note: a ban is an order forbidding something

explanation.surface: A court order is about to hold firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to stick' reads as 'about to stay', but 'about' is the containment and 'stick' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a stick, used by conductors, police or relay runners.

clue.text: Surreptitious foreign articles writing style

parts.note: un is a French article and der a German one
a hand is a style of handwriting

explanation.surface: Covert foreign newspaper pieces in a particular writing style.
explanation.definitionFit: Underhand means sly or secret, done deceitfully.

clue.text: Use fiction in a way that's easily picked up

indicators.note: in a way means in another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Writing fiction in a style that is readily caught by readers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infectious, like a disease or laughter, is readily caught from others.

clue.text: Rejected change to improve writing's flow

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to edit is to revise text to improve it

explanation.surface: A proposed revision was turned down because it spoilt the prose's rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide is the flow of the sea, as in a flowing or ebbing tide.

clue.text: Because of lock it's hard to break into

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in famous for
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Thanks to its lock, a building is tough to burgle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortress is a stronghold built to resist attackers getting in.

clue.text: More than one stiff blow received in grammar school

indicators.note: received in means taken inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a oner is a heavy blow in old slang

explanation.surface: A heavy punch landed in a grammar school fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stiff' is a noun here, slang for a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffs are corpses, and goners are people dead or beyond saving.

clue.text: Spare money for nursing hospital

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tin is old slang for money
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Spare cash set aside for nursing in a hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare as an adjective can mean lean or slight in build.

clue.text: Gives swimmer greeting

parts.note: hands means passes or gives
a hake is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: Someone welcomes a swimmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking hands is a common form of greeting.

clue.text: Poetic words used in parting on active service abroad

indicators.note: verse is used to split, or part, the other letters

parts.note: OAS is the military abbreviation for on active service
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Lines of poetry quoted when soldiers posted abroad say goodbye.
explanation.definitionFit: Overseas as an adverb means in foreign lands across the sea.

clue.text: Violated law — is sentence halved showing bias?

indicators.note: a violated law is broken, so the letters are rearranged
halved keeps only the first half of the word sentence

explanation.surface: A law was broken, so is a reduced sentence a sign of prejudice?
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' cuts SENTENCE to SENT, which joins LAW and IS in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Slantwise means at an angle, slanted, and so figuratively biased.

clue.text: Jewel box king's given upstart relative, in short

parts.note: to spar is to box
K is the chess abbreviation for king

indicators.note: in a down clue, upstart means the word is set going upwards

parts.note: rel is short for relative

explanation.surface: A jewellery box belonging to the king passes to a jumped-up relation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkler is slang for a diamond or other gem.

clue.text: I had to follow international agent without fear

indicators.note: to follow puts this piece after the others

parts.note: a rep is a sales agent
I'd contracts I had

explanation.surface: I had to tail a fearless foreign spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and bold.

clue.text: Car that's sound with nothing missing

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: audio means sound
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A car that runs well with nothing absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like praise for the car but gives AUDIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Audi is a German make of motor car.

clue.text: Sack a gunner involved in abuse

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so these pieces sit within the other

parts.note: mud is abuse, as in slinging mud
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: A soldier is dismissed for being caught up in mistreatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sack' is a verb, to plunder, not to dismiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To maraud is to raid and plunder, just as to sack a town is.

clue.text: What may get you to sleep picking up Amis's latest book

indicators.note: picking up means taking on board, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.words: What may get you to sleep
parts.note: ether was an early anaesthetic

indicators.note: latest picks the final letter of the word Amis's

explanation.surface: A sleep aid that comes with Martin Amis's newest novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: The man will meet destiny as slave

parts.note: he refers to a man
one's lot is one's fate

explanation.surface: A man will meet his fate as a slave.
explanation.definitionFit: Helots were the serfs of ancient Sparta, hence any slave.

clue.text: I once laboured with tax demand that's excessive

indicators.note: laboured suggests worked over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Someone recalls toiling under a punishing tax bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An exaction is an extortionate demand, as of money or tribute.

clue.text: Veteran keeps religious books readily available

indicators.note: keeps means holds, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: an OAP, old age pensioner, is a veteran
NT is the New Testament

explanation.surface: A pensioner keeps scripture close at hand.
explanation.definitionFit: On tap means available whenever needed, like beer from a barrel.

clue.text: Train weaker batsmen

definitions.meaning: a train is the trailing part, as of a gown or comet
in cricket, the lower-order batsmen are the bottom of the order

explanation.surface: Coach the poorer hitters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' is a noun, the trailing part, not coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are the back end: a trailing train, and the last batsmen in cricket.

clue.text: Artist in Baltic country reserves opera

indicators.note: in places the painter inside the country

parts.note: Latvia is a Baltic state
RA is a Royal Academician
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A painter in Latvia books seats for the opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reserves' is a noun here, the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: La Traviata is Verdi's opera about the courtesan Violetta.

clue.text: One blustering clergyman gets tip off when that woman's around

indicators.note: around means the pronoun surrounds the other piece

parts.note: her refers to that woman

indicators.note: tip off removes the first letter

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A ranting vicar loses his temper when a woman is near.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that woman's around' means 'that woman is around', so the pronoun wraps the shortened clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully and bluster, so one who does so blusters.

clue.text: Exercise after swim around English Channel resort

indicators.note: after puts the exercise piece behind the swim
around means the swim surrounds the letter for English

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: Working out after a swim around the English Channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Dieppe is a French port and resort on the English Channel.
